home.lead: A Brown Cocktail Pub in a house from 1734, in the alley between Singel and Spuistraat.
home.impBody1: Batavia is a living room for Amsterdammers, cocktail lovers, foodies and wine drinkers. Informal and snug: one table settles in for dinner, the next drops by for a drink.
home.impBody2: We work together with local farmers, producers and distillers to make our cocktails and dishes. Every menu is seasonal, and you can find all the information about the products we use on our menus.
home.peopleText: Batavia belongs to Samuel Stok and Jimmy Hu, two bartenders who met behind the same Amsterdam bar. Jimmy reached the top three of Best Bartender Netherlands 2024.
home.k1Text: Just walk in. To be sure of a table, book ahead.
home.k2Text: In good weather the terrace is out, with room for fifteen guests.
home.k4Text: Whether you come in for an alcoholic or a non-alcoholic drink, we have a unique selection of homemade non-alcoholic cocktails made with local products.
home.alleyBody: Lijnbaanssteeg is a narrow alley in the old centre, between Singel and Spuistraat. You'll find us at numbers 5–7, about ten minutes on foot from Centraal Station.

building.title: The building
building.lead: Lijnbaanssteeg 5–7 was built in 1734. Since then it has housed a commercial printing works, two restaurants and a cocktail bar. Now it is a public house.
building.nameText: Batavia is the old Latin name for the Netherlands. And public house, because we are a pub in an old Amsterdam house, open to everyone. No more, no less.
building.streetText: The alley takes its name from the lijnbanen, the rope-walks that lay here at the end of the sixteenth century, when Singel was still the edge of the city.
building.insideText: You can still see it inside: beams that were once part of ships, a natural stone floor and an antique bar.

timeline.title: The building
timeline.text: The building at Lijnbaanssteeg 5–7 is built.

timeline.title: The printing works
timeline.text: A commercial printing works runs at number 5. Its name is lettered large above the shopfront.

timeline.title: Restaurant Gravenmolen
timeline.text: In 1968 architect Nic. Klok draws the conversion: a taproom downstairs, the restaurant above. Gravenmolen opens in November 1969 and holds a Michelin star from 1972 to 1976.

timeline.title: De Jonge Gravenmolen
timeline.text: A new generation: restaurant De Jonge Gravenmolen.

timeline.title: Tales & Spirits

timeline.title: Batavia Public House
timeline.text: Today the doors open as Batavia Public House.
